<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>

output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% Transformation rule:
%   1. Find a maximal rectangle R1..R2 × C1..C2 of non‑zero cells
%      such that every row of the rectangle contains a non‑zero and
%      every column of the rectangle contains a non‑zero.
%   2. The rectangle is called the component rectangle.
%   3. Transpose the component rectangle: a cell (r,c,V) with
%      r1 ≤ r ≤ r2 , c1 ≤ c ≤ c2 becomes
%          (c1 + (c‑c1) , r1 + (r‑r1)) with the same colour V.
%   4. The transposed rectangle (size h'×w' where h'=width, w'=height)
%      is placed at a position (pRow,pCol) where the whole target region
%      does not intersect any component cell (i.e. no component cell lies
%      in [pRow..pRow+h'‑1]×[pRow..pCol+w'‑1]).
%   5. The output consists of the transposed values in that target
%      region and 0 everywhere else.
% ------------------------------------------------------------

% domain size – derived from the automatically injected facts
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% non‑zero cells
% ------------------------------------------------------------
non_zero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 1. Candidate rectangle:
%    every row and every column inside must contain a non‑zero
% ------------------------------------------------------------
rect_candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2) :-
    % each row in the interval must have a non‑zero in the column interval
    not exists R where
        R1 =< R, R =< R2,
        #count{C : non_zero(R,C), C1 =< C, C =< C2} = 0,
    % each column in the interval must have a non‑zero in the row interval
    not exists C where
        C1 =< C, C =< C2,
        #count{R : non_zero(R,C), R1 =< R, R =< R2} = 0.

% count of non‑zero cells inside a rectangle
count_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2,NC) :- 
    NC = #count{R,C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0,
                 R1 =< R, R =< R2, C1 =< C, C =< C2}.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 2. Component rectangle = rectangle with maximal non‑zero count
% ------------------------------------------------------------
max_cnt(MC) :- 
    MC = #max{Rc : 
                 #count{R,C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0,
                       R1 =< R, R =< R2, C1 =< C, C =< C2}
                 where rect_candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2)}.

component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2) :-
    rect_candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    count_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc),
    Nc = max_cnt.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 3. Dimensions of the component rectangle
% ------------------------------------------------------------
height = R2 - R1 + 1.
width  = C2 - C1 + 1.

% transposed dimensions (swap height ↔ width)
trans_h = width.
trans_w = height.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 4. Choose a placement (pRow,pCol) for the transposed rectangle
% ------------------------------------------------------------
placement(pRow,pCol) :-
    % fit into the grid
    pRow = #min(0, n_rows(N) - trans_h),
    pCol = #min(0, n_cols(N) - trans_w),
    pRow = #max(0, pRow),
    pCol = #max(0, pCol),
    % ensure the whole region is inside the board
    0 =< pRow, pRow + trans_h - 1 < n_rows(N),
    0 =< pCol, pCol + trans_w - 1 < n_cols(N),
    % no component cell may be overwritten
    not exists RC,V where
        component_cell(R,C,V),
        R1 =< R, R =< R2,
        C1 =< C, C =< C2,
        pRow =< R, R =< pRow + trans_h - 1,
        pCol =< C, C =< pCol + trans_w - 1.

% component cell predicate – cells that belong to the component rectangle
component_cell(R,C,V) :-
    non_zero(R,C,V),
    R1 =< R, R =< R2,
    C1 =< C, C =< C2.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 5. Output generation
% ------------------------------------------------------------
output(R,C,Val) :-
    % target region – a transposed copy of a component cell
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,Val),
    R = pRow + (Cc - C1),
    C = pCol + (Rc - R1),
    R = #placementRow,
    C = #placementCol,
    0 =< R, R < n_rows(N),
    0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).
% all other cells are zero
output(R,C,0) :- not output(R,C,_).

% exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R, C, Colour) : colour(Colour) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% domain size
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% component rectangle detection
candidate_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2) :-
    R1 =< R2, C1 =< C2,
    not exists R ( R1 =< R, R =< R2,
        #count{C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0, C1 =< C, C =< C2} = 0 ),
    not exists C ( C1 =< C, C =< C2,
        #count{R,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0, R1 =< R, R =< R2} = 0 ).

rect_count(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc) :-
    Nc = #count{R,C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0,
                R1 =< R, R =< R2,
                C1 =< C, C =< C2}.

max_nonzero(Mc) :-
    Mc = #max{Rc :
          #count{R,C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0,
                R1 =< R, R =< R2,
                C1 =< C, C =< C2},
          where candidate_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2)}.

component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2) :-
    candidate_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    rect_count(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc),
    Nc = max_nonzero(Mc).

component_cell(R,C,Vc) :-
    input(R,C,Vc), Vc != 0,
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    R1 =< R, R =< R2,
    C1 =< C, C =< C2.

output(R,C,Vc) :-
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,Vc),
    R = R2 + (C2 - C1) + (Rc - R1),
    C = C2 + (R2 - R1) + (Cc - C1),
    0 =< R, R < n_rows(N),
    0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

output_region(R,C) :-
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,Vc),
    R = R2 + (C2 - C1) + (Rc - R1),
    C = C2 + (R2 - R1) + (Cc - C1).

% Cells not in the transposed region must be zero
:- output(R,C,Color), Color != 0,
    not output_region(R,C).

% All cells must appear in output (either from mapping or zero)
cell(R,C) :- 0 =< R, R < n_rows(N), 0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- cell(R,C).

<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>

% count rows and cols
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% non-zero
non_zero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

% candidate rectangle
rect_candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2) :-
    R1 =< R2, C1 =< C2,
    % each row in interval must have a non-zero
    not exists R ( R1 =< R, R =< R2,
        #count{C,V : non_zero(R,C,V), C1 =< C, C =< C2} = 0),
    % each column in interval must have a non-zero
    not exists C ( C1 =< C, C =< C2,
        #count{R,V : non_zero(R,C,V), R1 =< R, R =< R2} = 0).

% count of non-zero cells in rectangle
rect_count(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc) :-
    Nc = #count{R,C,V : non_zero(R,C,V), R1 =< R, R =< R2, C1 =< C, C =< C2}.

% max count of any candidate rectangle
max_nonzero(M) :-
    M = #max{Rc :
        #count{R,C,V : non_zero(R,C,V), R1 =< R, R =< R2, C1 =< C, C =< C2},
        where rect_candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2)}.

% component rectangle (the rectangle that satisfies candidate and has maximal count)
component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2) :-
    rect_candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    rect_count(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc),
    Nc = max_nonzero(Max).

% component cells (non-zero cells inside component rectangle)
component_cell(R,C,V) :-
    non_zero(R,C,V),
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    R1 =< R, R =< R2,
    C1 =< C, C =< C2.

% dimensions of transposed rectangle
trans_h(Th) :- Th = C2 - C1 + 1.
trans_w(Tw) :- Tw = R2 - R1 + 1.

% placement (top-left of transposed rectangle)
pRow(Pr) :- Pr = R2 + (C2 - C1).
pCol(Pc) :- Pc = C2 + (R2 - R1).

% output for transposed cells
output(R,C,Vc) :-
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,Vc),
    R = pRow + (Cc - C1),
    C = pCol + (Rc - R1),
    0 =< R, R < n_rows(N),
    0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

% output for original component rectangle (unchanged)

    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,Vc),
    R = Rc - R1,
    C = Cc - C1,
    0 =< R, R < n_rows(N),
    0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

% all other cells must be zero

% cell domain
cell(R,C) :- 0 =< R, R < n_rows(N), 0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

% Define rows and cols
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% non-zero
non_zero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

% bounding rectangle of non-zero cells
#min{R : non_zero(R,_,_)} = Rmin.
#max{R : non_zero(R,_,_)} = Rmax.
#min{C : non_zero(_,C,_) } = Cmin.
#max{C : non_zero(_,C,_) } = Cmax.

% component rectangle
component_rect(Rmin,Rmax,Cmin,Cmax) :-
    #min{R : non_zero(R,_,_)} = Rmin,
    #max{R : non_zero(R,_,_)} = Rmax,
    #min{C : non_zero(_,C,_) } = Cmin,
    #max{C : non_zero(_,C,_) } = Cmax.

% component cell
component_cell(Rc,Cc,V) :-
    non_zero(Rc,Cc,V),
    component_rect(Rmin,Rmax,Cmin,Cmax),
    Rmin =< Rc, Rc =< Rmax,
    Cmin =< Cc, Cc =< Cmax.

% original output (copy original rectangle unchanged)
output(R,C,V) :-
    component_rect(Rmin,Rmax,Cmin,Cmax),
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,V),
    R = Rc,
    C = Cc,
    0 =< R, R < n_rows(N),
    0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

% transposed output (swap axes)
output_trans(R,C,V) :-
    component_rect(Rmin,Rmax,Cmin,Cmax),
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,V),
    R = Rmax + (Cmax - Cmin) + (Cc - Cmin),
    C = Cmax + (Rmax - Rmin) + (Rc - Rmin),
    0 =< R, R < n_rows(N),
    0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

% uncovered cells become zero
output(R,C,0) :-
    component_rect(Rmin,Rmax,Cmin,Cmax),
    not covered(R,C),
    0 =< R, R < n_rows(N),
    0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

% covered predicate
covered(R,C) :- covered_original(R,C) ; covered_trans(R,C).

% covered_original
covered_original(R,C) :-
    component_rect(Rmin,Rmax,Cmin,Cmax),
    non_zero(R,C,V),
    Rmin =< R, R =< Rmax,
    Cmin =< C, C =< Cmax.

% covered_trans
covered_trans(R,C) :-
    component_rect(Rmin,Rmax,Cmin,Cmax),
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,V),
    R = Rmax + (Cmax - Cmin) + (Cc - Cmin),
    C = Cmax + (Rmax - Rmin) + (Rc - Rmin).

% cell domain
cell(R,C) :- 0 =< R, R < n_rows(N), 0 =< C, C < n_cols(N).

% Exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R,C,Colour) : colour(Colour) } 1 :- cell(R,C).

%   1. Find a maximal rectangle R1..R2 × C1..C2 of non‑zero cells
%      such that every row of the rectangle contains a non‑zero and
%      every column of the rectangle contains a non‑zero.
%   2. The rectangle is called the component rectangle.
%   3. Transpose the component rectangle: a cell (r,c,V) with
%      r1 ≤ r ≤ r2 , c1 ≤ c ≤ c2 becomes
%          (c1 + (c‑c1) , r1 + (r‑r1)) with the same colour V.
%   4. The transposed rectangle (size h'×w' where h'=width, w'=height)
%      is placed at a position (pRow,pCol) where the whole target region
%      does not intersect any component cell (i.e. no component cell lies
%      in [pRow..pRow+h'‑1]×[pRow..pCol+w'‑1]).
%   5. The output consists of the transposed values in that target
%      region and 0 everywhere else.

n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

    not exists R where
        R1 =< R, R =< R2,
        #count{C : non_zero(R,C), C1 =< C, C =< C2} = 0,
    % each column in the interval must have a non‑zero in the row interval
    not exists C where
        C1 =< C, C =< C2,
        #count{R : non_zero(R,C), R1 =< R, R =< R2} = 0.

% count of non‑zero cells inside a rectangle
count_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2,NC) :- 
    NC = #count{R,C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0,
                 R1 =< R, R =< R2, C1 =< C, C =< C2}.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 2. Component rectangle = rectangle with maximal non‑zero count
% ------------------------------------------------------------
max_cnt(MC) :- 
    MC = #max{Rc : 
                 #count{R,C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0,

    rect_candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    count_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc),
    Nc = max_cnt.

% ------------------------------------------------------------

    pCol = #min(0, n_cols(N) - trans_w),

    pCol = #max(0, pCol),
    % ensure the whole region is inside the board
    0 =< pRow, pRow + trans_h - 1 < n_rows(N),
    0 =< pCol, pCol + trans_w - 1 < n_cols(N),
    % no component cell may be overwritten

        R1 =< R, R =< R2,
        C1 =< C, C =< C2,

% Dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% Non-zero cells
non_zero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

% Candidate rectangle: each row and column in the rectangle has a non-zero
candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2) :-
    R1 =< R2, C1 =< C2,
    not exists R where R1 =< R, R =< R2,
        #count{C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0, C1 =< C, C =< C2} = 0,
    not exists C where C1 =< C, C =< C2,
        #count{R,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0, R1 =< R, R =< R2} = 0.

% Count of non-zero cells in a rectangle
rect_count(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc) :-
    Nc = #count{R,C,V : input(R,C,V), V != 0,
                 R1 =< R, R =< R2,
                 C1 =< C, C =< C2}.

% Component rectangle = maximal candidate rectangle
component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2) :-
    candidate(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    rect_count(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc),
    not exists R1b,R2b,C1b,C2b,Countb where
        candidate(R1b,R2b,C1b,C2b),
        rect_count(R1b,R2b,C1b,C2b,Countb),
        Countb > rect_count(R1,R2,C1,C2,Nc).

% Component cell (non-zero inside the component rectangle)
component_cell(Rc,Cc,Vc) :-
    input(Rc,Cc,Vc), Vc != 0,
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    R1 =< Rc, Rc =< R2,
    C1 =< Cc, Cc =< C2.

% Grid dimensions for later use
N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
M = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% Component rectangle dimensions
height = R2 - R1 + 1.
width  = C2 - C1 + 1.

% Placement options (choose opposite diagonal quadrant)
% 1) component rectangle touches top and left -> copy goes to bottom-right
placement(PRow,PCol) :-
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    R1 = 0, C1 = 0,
    PRow = R2 + (C2 - C1),
    PCol = C2 + (R2 - R1).

% 2) component rectangle touches top and right -> copy goes to bottom-left
placement(PRow,PCol) :-
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    R1 = 0, C2 = M-1,
    PRow = R2 + (C2 - C1),
    PCol = C1 - (C2 - C1) - (R2 - R1).

% 3) component rectangle touches bottom and left -> copy goes to top-right
placement(PRow,PCol) :-
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    R2 = N-1, C1 != 0,
    PRow = R1 - (R2 - R1) - (C2 - C1) + 1,
    PCol = C1 + (R2 - R1).

% Copy of the component rectangle (normal orientation)
copy_pos(R,C,Vc) :-
    component_cell(Rc,Cc,Vc),
    component_rect(R1,R2,C1,C2),
    placement(PRow,PCol),
    R = PRow + (Rc - R1),
    C = PCol + (Cc - C1),
    0 =< R, R < N,
    0 =< C, C < M,
    not component_cell(R,C,_).

% Original component cells stay unchanged
output(Rc,Cc,Vc) :- component_cell(Rc,Cc,Vc).

% Copy cells
output(R,C,Vc) :- copy_pos(R,C,Vc).

% Cells that are not part of either should be zero
:- output(R,C,Col), Col != 0,
    not component_cell(R,C,_),
    not copy_pos(R,C,_).

% Every cell must be assigned a color
cell(R,C) :- 0 =< R, R < N, 0 =< C, C < M.

1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- cell(R,C).
```
